attribute_reduction.other: Redwood Fabrication, Inc. — Case No. 26-11842 (Bankr. D. Colo.); plan confirmed 9/2/2026 (Dkt. 214), effective date 9/30/2026. Measurement: allowed general unsecured claims $8,400,000 recovered at 35% cash ($2,940,000 over 24 months, first installment on the effective date — Dkt. 214 excerpt and plan term sheet); the remainder $8,400,000 − $2,940,000 = $5,460,000 is the 'balance discharged on the effective date' per the term sheet, and is both the COD income that would otherwise be includible and the amount excluded under 26 U.S.C. §108(a)(1)(A) because the discharge occurs in this title 11 case (library: irc_108.md). The tax measurement uses undiscounted principal amounts; present-value conventions for the tax computation are not covered by the reference library and were not relied on (the accounting presentation of the same payments is separate — see emergence_balance_sheet.md and QUESTIONS.md Q13). Attribute reduction under IRC §108(b)(1) (library: irc_108.md), applied after the tax for the year of discharge (2026) is determined: the entire $5,460,000 excluded amount goes to attribute (A), the NOL — the $6,100,000 federal NOL carryforward per prior returns (plan term sheet) is reduced to $640,000. Nothing remains, so attributes (B)–(G) — general business credits, minimum tax credit, capital loss carryovers, basis of property, passive activity loss carryovers, foreign tax credits — are not reduced, and the $3,200,000 tax basis in fixed assets (plan term sheet) is preserved. Assumptions/open items: (i) the NOL is measured at the petition-date carryforward; any NOL generated for the 2026 year of discharge is not in the record — QUESTIONS.md Q14(a); (ii) the record shows no other §108(b) attributes; if any exist, this schedule changes — QUESTIONS.md Q14(b); (iii) deferred-tax effects of the reduction are not quantifiable without rates — QUESTIONS.md Q14(c).

election_108b5: No. Under the default IRC §108(b)(1) order (library: irc_108.md) the reduction goes to the NOL first, and the $6,100,000 NOL exceeds the $5,460,000 exclusion, so the reduction ends inside the NOL: residual NOL $640,000 and the entire $3,200,000 of fixed-asset basis preserved, depreciation deductions flowing as before. Electing §108(b)(5) to apply the reduction first to depreciable-property basis would consume the full $3,200,000 of basis (assets in service at a fabricator with $14,000,000 enterprise value) and still leave $2,260,000 of excluded income to place; the library does not say where a remainder goes once depreciable basis is exhausted (unverified — would need confirmation before any election). Even on the favorable assumption that the $2,260,000 remainder then reduces the NOL, the election merely converts $3,200,000 of basis into $3,200,000 more NOL — aggregate face deduction unchanged (default: $640,000 NOL + $3,200,000 depreciable basis; election: $3,840,000 NOL + zero basis) — while shifting deductions from near-term, income-independent depreciation to an NOL usable only against future taxable income, whose carryforward limits are not in the record. Not advantageous on these facts; election declined. Revisit only if the attribute picture changes (QUESTIONS.md Q14).
